diagnostic:
S1 implemented as designed: a resuming run takes over the already-read rows of the plan it picks up. resume_plan now folds over every frozen row (not only the planned ones): a row stored read goes to the new Resume::already_read whatever the bio checks and removed sources say, a row stored skipped is no row of this run's plan, and the planned rows keep their existing read/carry/skip verdict. Resume::kept returns the new KeptRow { position, status } in plan order, read for a taken-over row and planned for one read now or carried. ScanRunPort::record_plan takes &[ScanPlanRow], the insert writes the given status instead of the literal 'planned', PlanRowStatus gained ALL and as_str beside parse (one owner for the stored vocabulary, as ScanStatus and AccountCheckOutcome already have), the scan task writes planned rows for a fresh plan and each kept row with its carried status for a resumed one, and the purge seed passes its row statuses. repos_read_of, mark_repo_read and the queue view are untouched.
GREEN (this Mac host): cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture exit 0, 6 passed (both journeys read "3 repos read"); cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure exit 0, 4 passed; cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store exit 0, 222 passed over 8 targets; cargo xtask check-arch exit 0 (30 members); cargo clippy over the four touched packages exit 0, no warning.
Tests added in the owned paths (host-authorised): review-domain repo_scope::tests::a_resume_keeps_as_read_exactly_the_rows_the_scan_already_read (L1, L2, L3 over any plan, checks and removals, including the carried share of Resume::kept) and adapter-review-store scan_runs::tests::a_plan_reads_back_with_the_statuses_it_was_written_with (L4 plus the read count the run reports). The three in-crate record_plan callers and the purge seed moved to ScanPlanRow with a named planned() helper; no assertion weakened, no oracle or support file touched.
Mutation (per-feature, in-diff over the modified production files): 12 mutants, 7 caught, 0 missed, 5 unviable. Kill rate 7/7 = 100% of viable, gate >= 80% met. review-domain + adapter-review-store 3 caught/1 unviable (cargo mutants -j 4, exit 0); ports/src/review.rs 4 caught/1 unviable with --test-package adapter-review-store (exit 0); openlore-review-app scan.rs 3 mutants all unviable (Ended and ResumedPlan have no Default, so the generated mutants do not compile), its behaviour covered by the acceptance journeys.
